text: cell.build refuses to create a cell whose ancestor directory chain contains CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .claude, .claude.json, or .mcp.json
how_i_tested: test_cell_sterility.py::BuildRefusalTests::test_contaminated_ancestor_blocks_the_build and ::test_ancestor_check_names_the_offending_file — both written this cycle, by me, in the same session as cell.py. Shown exercised by mutation: replacing `if contaminated:` with `if False and contaminated:` turns the suite red. That establishes the tests reach the guard, not that the guard is the right guard: whether the runner discovers context by walking upward from cwd was not tested and is ASSUMPTIONS.md item 13.

text: cell.census reports a cell as non-sterile when the filesystem walk finds any path that was not declared, any forbidden name at any depth, or any symlink
how_i_tested: test_cell_sterility.py::BuiltCellTests — six tests planting an undeclared file, a CLAUDE.md at the top level, a MEMORY.md two directories down, and a symlink pointing out of the cell; written this cycle, by me. Shown exercised by mutation: disabling the forbidden-name branch turns the suite red. Every plant is performed by the test itself, from the parent, with full permissions — no child process put anything there, so this is evidence about the walk, not about what a contained child can do.

text: attest.compare returns BYPASSED for a content change, a same-size content change, a created file, a removed file, a created empty directory, a file-mode change with identical content, a directory-mode change, a created symlink, a retargeted symlink, and a file replaced by a directory

The directory-mode case existed only after a mutation run showed nothing covered it, which is the one place this cycle's tests were demonstrably incomplete before being corrected.

text: attest.as_check maps INTACT to a PASS outcome and BYPASSED to a BYPASSED outcome, and for UNKNOWN emits no outcome key at all, so gauge.adjudicate reaches ACTIVE, BYPASSED and UNKNOWN respectively

text: A child process receives environment variables that the parent did not pass in subprocess env=: on Darwin 25.6 a CPython child additionally carries LC_CTYPE and __CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING, and a child reached through /usr/bin/python3 additionally carries CPATH, LIBRARY_PATH, MANPATH and SDKROOT
how_i_tested: Measured directly this cycle, by me, before any of it was written down: four spawns with env={HOME, PATH} through /bin/sh, /usr/bin/env, /usr/bin/python3 and the Homebrew python3.12, reading back the child's os.environ. /usr/bin/env arrived with exactly the two names passed, which is what isolates the additions to re-exec on the exec path rather than to env= being ignored. Pinned by test_launch_sterile_env.py::SpawnedChildTests::test_child_sees_the_sterile_environment_and_cwd, which asserts the observed floor equals launch.PLATFORM_INJECTED_ENV so a platform that adds a different name fails rather than passing quietly, and by ::test_a_shim_on_the_exec_path_adds_more_than_the_platform_does. This is a measurement on one host, on one OS version, by the party that benefits from it being interesting. It has not been reproduced by anyone else and was not measured on any other platform.

text: launch.BASE_PATH, chosen as a clean system PATH, resolves python3 to /usr/bin/python3 — the Command Line Tools stub that re-execs through xcrun and is the injecting shim of C-0009
how_i_tested: test_launch_sterile_env.py::SpawnedChildTests::test_the_modules_own_base_path_resolves_python3_to_the_shim — written this cycle, by me, after the first version of the baseline test accidentally routed through the shim and failed. The failure is how this was found; it was not predicted. No audit of what else on BASE_PATH re-execs has been done, so this names one instance of a class rather than the class.

text: manifest.render selects members by glob over *.py excluding test_* plus SPEC.md, ASSUMPTIONS.md and contract.json, so a Ring 0 module added later joins the sealed set without anyone listing it, and the emitted lines use the two-space separator machine.verify_manifest parses
how_i_tested: test_manifest.py — nine tests, written this cycle, by me, including one asserting the checked-in MANIFEST.sha256 equals a fresh render and one asserting cell.py, attest.py and launch.py are covered. MANIFEST.sha256 was regenerated by running manifest.py, never hand-edited; the six pre-existing hashes are byte-identical to before, which is what shows the change set touched only ASSUMPTIONS.md among previously-manifested files.

text: attest.compare cannot detect a write that was fully reverted before the post-attest was taken, including mode bits
how_i_tested: test_attest_delta.py::DeltaDetectionTests::test_chmod_out_and_back_with_nothing_left_is_not_detectable — written this cycle, by me. It asserts the miss: chmod the sealed directory open, create a file, delete it, chmod back, and compare reports INTACT. Raised as a claim rather than left in a docstring because it is a limit of the instrument SPEC §5 step 6 calls the honest one, and a limit that is only implied gets read as absent. Closing it needs a monitor during the run, not a manifest after it.

text: cell.attest_args rebases a CellSpec's home-relative scratch prefixes onto the cell root that attest.freeze walks, so a runner's write into a declared scratch region yields INTACT with the write recorded as a scratch delta, where passing the spec's prefixes through unrebased yields BYPASSED
how_i_tested: test_lifecycle_proof.py::ScratchDeclarationTests::test_a_declared_scratch_write_is_not_bypassed and ::test_the_rebased_prefix_is_the_one_attest_receives — both written this cycle, by me, in the same session as the cell.py change they exercise. Shown load-bearing rather than incidentally green: monkeypatching cell.attest_args back to the un-rebased form and stripping the new guard turns the first test red with exactly the reported symptom, 'BYPASSED' != 'INTACT'. That establishes the test reaches the defect. It does not establish that rebasing is the right repair as against freezing attest on cell.home instead, which was not tried.

text: attest.freeze at phase 'pre' raises AttestError when a declared scratch prefix matches no path in the tree being frozen, and does not perform that check at phase 'post'
how_i_tested: test_lifecycle_proof.py::ScratchDeclarationTests::test_handing_attest_the_raw_home_relative_prefix_now_fails_closed covers the pre-phase refusal, and ::test_a_removed_scratch_directory_is_a_delta_at_post_not_a_crash covers the post-phase exemption by removing a declared scratch directory between the two attestations and asserting the run survives with the removal reported as a scratch delta. Both written this cycle, by me. The exemption was shown load-bearing rather than incidental: on the identical post-removal tree, freeze('pre') raises and freeze('post') does not, so the phase test is what separates them. The second test asserts on attest directly rather than through a child, because a child would first have to clear the seal on the cell home and that chmod is itself an attested delta that would mask the behaviour under test — so it does not establish that a real runner removing its own scratch directory produces this result.

text: attest.compare returns INTACT, and attest.as_check maps that to outcome PASS, for a cell whose child process never executed — the integrity check is indistinguishable from a clean run

text: declaring the runner's own state directory '.claude' as a cell scratch prefix produces a cell that cell.census reports non-sterile on the forbidden-name check, so cell.require_sterile raises and launch.plan refuses before spawning
how_i_tested: Not covered by a committed test. I did not add a test because a test asserting this would read as endorsing it, and whether it is correct behaviour or a blocking defect is finding F-3, which is not mine to settle.

text: CellSpec.__post_init__ refuses a scratch prefix of '.' or '', which previously parsed to zero parts, skipped the evidence-tree check that indexes parts[0], and declared the entire cell home as scratch — so evidence inside the cell could be rewritten between pre and post attestation while attest.compare returned INTACT and as_check returned outcome PASS
how_i_tested: test_lifecycle_proof.py::ScratchDeclarationTests::test_a_scratch_prefix_naming_the_home_itself_is_refused and ::test_the_evidence_tree_cannot_be_declared_scratch_by_any_spelling — written this cycle, by me, in the same session as the cell.py change. The defect was demonstrated before it was fixed rather than argued: a cell built with scratch_prefixes=('.',) and one evidence file had that file's contents replaced with 'TAMPERED' between the two attestations, and compare returned INTACT with delta_count 0, the content change filed under scratch_deltas. Found by a Temper pass over my own change, not by the change's own tests — the tests I wrote for C-0013 would not have caught it, because they only exercise well-formed prefixes.
